grades.quote: sys_link creates a new name for an existing inode.
grades.reason: It describes how xv6 implements hard links (sys_link creates a new directory entry for an existing inode and increments ip->nlink). That is background on hard-link mechanics. It never says what happens to a hard link or a symbolic link when the original pathname is removed.

grades.quote: symbolic links (or soft links) are pathnames that do not refer directly to a file, but rather indirectly to whatever another pathname refers to.
grades.reason: It uses DNS aliases as an analogy and briefly says symbolic links refer indirectly to whatever another pathname refers to. It does not discuss removal of the original name or the resulting behavior.

grades.quote: then you would have a dangling reference
grades.reason: It says directly that unlinking the target name leaves a symbolic link as a dangling reference, because the link refers to another name rather than to the file. It also contrasts hard and symbolic links, and shows two names leading to the same file. It never states outright that a hard link keeps the file accessible after the original name is removed, so the hard-link side is only implied.
